section.content: 本公开的示例涉及产生训练或校准数据以供机器学习接收器使用。在一些示例中，数据节点从机器学习节点接收对生成随机比特序列的能力的指示。数据节点向机器学习节点发送用于生成随机比特序列的一个或多个参数。参数符合所指示的能力。数据节点还发送随机比特序列，其中随机比特序列根据所发送的参数被生成。

Examples of the present disclosure relate to generating training or calibration data for use by a machine learning receiver. In some examples, the data node receives an indication of an ability to generate a random bit sequence from the machine learning node. The data node sends one or more parameters for generating a random bit sequence to the machine learning node. The parameters conform to the indicated capabilities. The data node also transmits a random bit sequence, wherein the random bit sequence is generated according to the transmitted parameters.

Machine learning receiverTechnical Field

Examples of the present disclosure relate to Machine Learning (ML) receivers. Some involve generating training data or calibration data for use by the ML receiver.

Background

Receivers within a communication network may use an ML model to improve the performance of the receiver. The ML model may be used for physical layer processing or for any other suitable function. For example, the ML model may be used to perform tasks such as channel estimation and equalization.

Disclosure of Invention

According to various (but not necessarily all) examples of the disclosure there is provided a data node comprising means for:

receiving an indication of an ability to generate a random bit sequence from a machine learning node;

Transmitting one or more parameters for generating a random bit sequence to a machine learning node, wherein the parameters conform to the indicated capabilities, and

A random bit sequence is transmitted, wherein the random bit sequence is generated according to the transmitted parameters.

The one or more parameters may include at least one of:

One or more random number generator algorithms;

a seed of the random number generator;

The length of the random bit sequence to be generated.

The random bit sequence may include training data for training a machine learning model in the machine learning node.

The random bit sequence may be transmitted as desired.

The random bit sequence may be transmitted using a pattern defined in the indicated capability.

The random bit sequence may be broadcast to two or more machine learning nodes.

The means may be for measuring resource usage during the time interval and transmitting a random bit sequence if the resource usage is below a threshold.

The random bit sequence may be mapped directly to the transmitted symbol.

The data node may comprise one of:

A user equipment;

An access node.

According to various (but not necessarily all) examples of the disclosure there is provided a method comprising:

receiving an indication of an ability to generate a random bit sequence from a machine learning node;

Transmitting one or more parameters for generating a random bit sequence to a machine learning node, wherein the parameters conform to the indicated capabilities, and

A random bit sequence is transmitted, wherein the random bit sequence is generated according to the transmitted parameters.

According to various (but not necessarily all) examples of the disclosure there is provided a computer program comprising instructions that, when executed by a data node, cause the data node to at least perform:

receiving an indication of an ability to generate a random bit sequence from a machine learning node;

Transmitting one or more parameters for generating a random bit sequence to a machine learning node, wherein the parameters conform to the indicated capabilities, and

A random bit sequence is transmitted, wherein the random bit sequence is generated according to the transmitted parameters.

According to various (but not necessarily all) examples of the disclosure there is provided a machine learning node comprising means for:

Transmitting an indication of the ability to generate a random bit sequence to a data node;

Receiving one or more parameters from a data node for generating a random bit sequence, wherein the received parameters conform to the indicated capabilities, and

A random bit sequence is received from the data node, wherein the random bit sequence includes training data for training a machine learning model in the machine learning node.

These components may be used to annotate the received random bit sequence with a random bit sequence generated with the received one or more parameters such that the annotated data may be used to train a machine learning model.

These components may be used to store a received original signal that includes a transmitted bit sequence.

These components may be used to train a machine learning model using the stored raw signals as input.

The machine learning model may be trained to estimate the probability of the received bits.

These components may be used to demodulate the received signal and record the received random bit sequence after demodulation.

These components may be used to send a request for a random bit sequence to a data node.

The request may include at least one of:

A random number generator algorithm to be used;

The state of the random number generator algorithm to be used;

The length of the random bit sequence to be generated;

the transmit power level to be used for signals comprising random bit sequences.

The machine learning node may include one of:

A user equipment;

An access node.

According to various (but not necessarily all) examples of the disclosure there is provided a method comprising:

Transmitting an indication of the ability to generate a random bit sequence to a data node;

Receiving one or more parameters from a data node for generating a random bit sequence, wherein the received parameters conform to the indicated capabilities, and

A random bit sequence is received from the data node, wherein the random bit sequence includes training data for training a machine learning model in the machine learning node.

According to various (but not necessarily all) examples of the disclosure there is provided a computer program comprising instructions that, when executed by a machine learning node, cause the machine learning node to at least perform:

Transmitting an indication of the ability to generate a random bit sequence to a data node;

Receiving one or more parameters from a data node for generating a random bit sequence, wherein the received parameters conform to the indicated capabilities, and

A random bit sequence is received from the data node, wherein the random bit sequence includes training data for training a machine learning model in the machine learning node.

While the above examples and optional features of the disclosure have been described separately, it is to be understood that they are included within the disclosure in all possible combinations and permutations of arrangements. It should be understood that the various examples of the disclosure may include any or all of the features described with respect to other examples of the disclosure, and vice versa. Furthermore, it will be understood that any one or more or all of the features of any combination may be implemented/embodied by/included in/performed by an apparatus, method and/or computer program instructions, as needed and/or appropriate.

Drawings

Some examples will now be described with reference to the accompanying drawings, in which:

FIG. 1 illustrates an exemplary network;

FIG. 2 illustrates an example ML receiver;

FIGS. 3A and 3B illustrate an exemplary method;

FIG. 4 illustrates an exemplary method;

FIG. 5 illustrates an exemplary method;

FIG. 6 illustrates an exemplary physical layer mapping;

FIG. 7 illustrates an exemplary method;

FIG. 8 illustrates an exemplary method, and

Fig. 9 illustrates an exemplary controller.

The figures are not necessarily drawn to scale. Certain features and aspects of the drawings may be shown schematically or exaggerated in scale for clarity and conciseness. For example, the dimensions of some of the elements in the figures may be exaggerated relative to other elements to help improve the description. Corresponding reference numerals are used in the drawings to indicate corresponding features. For purposes of clarity, not all reference numbers are necessarily shown in all figures.

Definition of the definition

Detailed Description

Fig. 1 shows an example of a communication network 100, such as a 5G network or a 6G network, or any other suitable type of network. The network 100 comprises a plurality of nodes 110, 120, 130 of different types. The different types of nodes 110, 120, 130 may include end nodes 110 and network nodes 120, 130. The network nodes may include access node 120 and core network node 130, and/or any other suitable type of device.

Access node 120 may be configured to communicate with end node 110. The core network node 130 communicates with the access node 120. In some examples, core network node 130 communicates with end node 110.

In some examples, core network nodes 130 may communicate with each other. In some examples, one or more access nodes 120 may communicate with each other.

Network 100 may be a cellular network including a plurality of cells 122. Each cell is served by an access node 120. In this example, the interface between the terminal node 110 and the access node 120 defining the cell 122 is a wireless interface 124.

Access node 120 may include one or more cellular radio transceivers. End node 110 may include one or more cellular radio transceivers.

Access node 120 may be a base station. Access node 120 may be any suitable type of base station. Access node 120 may be a network entity responsible for radio transmission and reception to and from end node 110 in one or more cells. The access node 120 may be a network element in a Radio Access Network (RAN) or any other suitable type of network.

The core network node 130 may be part of a core network. The core network node 130 may be configured to manage functionality related to the connection of the UE 110. For example, the core network node 130 may be configured to manage functions such as connectivity, mobility, authentication, authorization, and/or other suitable functions.

In the example of fig. 1, the core network node 130 is shown as a single entity. In some examples, the core network node 130 may be distributed across multiple entities. For example, the core network nodes 130 may be cloud-based, or distributed in any other suitable manner.

One or more nodes in network 100 may be configured to use an ML model. The ML model may be configured to improve the performance of various nodes within the network 100. For example, an ML receiver may be a node that receives a signal and performs processing tasks on the received signal using an ML model. The processing task may be channel estimation or equalization, or any other suitable task. The ML receiver may be a terminal node 110, such as a User Equipment (UE), or an access node 120, such as a gndeb (gNB), or any other suitable type of node.

The ML model may include a neural network or any other suitable model. In some examples, the ML model may be implemented using a trainable computer program. A trainable computer program may include any program that may be trained to perform one or more tasks without being explicitly programmed to perform those tasks.

The ML model used within the ML receiver may include a neural network, or any other suitable type of trainable model. The term "machine learning model" refers to any kind of Artificial Intelligence (AI), agent, or other method that can be trained or refined using data. The ML model may comprise a computer program. The ML model may be trained to perform tasks such as channel estimation or equalization without being explicitly programmed to perform the tasks. The ML model may be configured to learn from experience E in certain aspects of task T and performance metrics P if its performance in task T (as measured by P) improves with experience E. In these examples, the ML model may typically be learned from training data or calibration data to estimate future data. The ML model may also be a trainable computer program. In other examples, other types of ML models may be used.

It is also possible to train an ML model with a specific architecture and then derive another ML model from the ML model using processes such as compilation, pruning, quantization or distillation. The term ML model also covers all these use cases and their outputs. The ML model may be performed using any suitable means, such as CPU, GPU, ASIC, FPGA, in-memory computing, analog or digital, or optical means. The ML model may also be implemented in a device that combines any number of features in these devices, such as a digital-optical mixer or an analog-digital mixer. In some examples, the weights and required calculations in these systems may be programmed to correspond to an ML model. In some examples, the apparatus may be designed and manufactured to perform the tasks defined by the ML model, such that the apparatus is configured to perform the tasks when it is manufactured, without the apparatus being programmable.

Fig. 2 illustrates an exemplary ML model 200 that may be used in an ML receiver. In other examples, other types of ML models may be used.

The exemplary ML model 200 may be used for single-input and single-output (SISO) scenarios. In this example, the ML model 200 is a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) of the residual network (ResNet) type. The input 202 to the ML model 200 is a Time Transmission Interval (TTI). The TTI includes N symb OFDM symbols. The number of OFDM symbols is typically 14. The TTI includes N sc subcarriers.

The input 202 to the ML model 200 includes two channels. The first input channel 204 comprises a complex valued received signal and the second input channel 206 comprises a complex valued raw channel estimate. Thus, the input 202 to the ML model 200 includes an N sc×Nsymb x 4 array of real values. In this array, the last dimension represents the number of input channels.

In other examples, ML model 200 may be used for a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) scenario. In such examples, the channel matrix may be vectorized along the channel dimension. This results in N LNR raw channel estimates per resource element, where N L is the number of layers and N R is the number of Rx antennas (accordingly, the received OFDM symbol array will include N R samples per resource element).

The ML model 200 is configured such that the input array is processed with one or more ResNet blocks 210. The convolutionally concatenated layer may be omitted if the number of channels between two consecutive ResNet blocks 210 is the same.

One ResNet block 210 is shown in fig. 2. ResNet block 210 may be repeated M times. The input for ResNet blocks i is the output of ResNet blocks i-1. In the example of fig. 2. N sc is the number of received subcarriers over the active bandwidth portion, N symb is the number of OFDM symbols in the slot (typically 14), N 1…Nj+k+l is the number of output channels in the convolutional layer within each ResNet block 210, and N B is the number of bits per Resource Element (RE).

The ML model 200 is configured such that the output of ResNet blocks 210 is fed to the final two-dimensional convolution layer 212. The final two-dimensional convolution layer 212 provides a final log-likelihood ratio (LLR) estimate as an output 214. The LLR estimates are probabilistic estimates of the transmitted bits by the ML receiver. The originally transmitted bits represent the ideal output of the ML model 200.

The ML model 200 may be trained using simulation data, in which case it is not problematic to obtain the originally transmitted sequence. However, there are scenarios where the ML model 200 may require training data collected in the network. Examples of the present disclosure provide a mechanism for an ML receiver to obtain originally transmitted bits so that the originally transmitted bits can be used to train the ML model 200.

In order to train a robust ML model for an ML receiver, the bit sequence used to generate the training data must be random. If there are only a limited number of previously agreed training bit sequences, the model will always be over fitted, predicting only those sequences. Examples of the present disclosure ensure that the originally transmitted bits comprise a random bit sequence.

Fig. 3A and 3B illustrate exemplary methods that may be used in examples of the present disclosure. The method of fig. 3A may be implemented by a data node and the method of fig. 3B may be implemented by an ML node. A data node is a node that transmits a random bit sequence. The data nodes may provide data that may be used to train the ML model 200. An ML node is a node that uses one or more ML models. The ML node may be an ML receiver, or any other suitable type of node. The ML node may receive data from the data node and use the received data to train the ML model. The data node may be a user equipment or an access node. Similarly, the ML node may be a user equipment or an access node.

In the example of fig. 3A, the method includes, at block 300, receiving an indication of an ability to generate a random bit sequence from an ML node. The indication of the capability may be received as part of a configuration process, or using any other suitable type of signaling.

At block 302, the method includes transmitting one or more parameters for generating a random bit sequence to an ML node. The transmitted parameters conform to the indicated capabilities.

The parameters include information that can be used to generate a random bit sequence. Parameters may be used to ensure that both the ML node and the data node generate the same random bit sequence.

In some examples, the parameters may include parameters related to a Random Number Generator (RNG). In some examples, the parameters may include one or more RNG algorithms, a seed of the RNG, a length of a random bit sequence to be generated, and/or any other suitable parameters.

In some examples, there may be a pre-configuration process in which a respective node is configured with one or more RNGs. In such an example, the index of available RNGs may be agreed upon during pre-configuration. In such examples, the parameters may include a reference to an index to indicate the RNG algorithm to be used.

The method further includes transmitting a random bit sequence at block 304. A random bit sequence is generated based on the transmitted parameters.

The random bit sequence includes training data that can be used to train an ML model in the ML node.

The random bit sequence may be transmitted in any suitable manner. In some examples, the random bit sequence may be transmitted on demand. The data for transmission may be scheduled via control signaling. In some examples, the random bit sequence may be transmitted using a pattern defined in the indicated capabilities. In some examples, the random bit sequence may be broadcast to two or more ML nodes. In some examples, the data node may measure resource usage during the time interval. If the resource usage is below the threshold, a random bit sequence may be sent.

The random bit sequence may be mapped directly to the transmitted symbol. This may enable omitting the step of physical layer mapping. For example, steps such as code block segmentation and code block concatenation may be omitted.

FIG. 3B illustrates an exemplary method that may be performed by an ML node. The ML node performing the method of fig. 3B may be a node corresponding to a data node performing the method of fig. 3A. That is, the data generated by the data node of fig. 3A may transmit a random bit sequence to the ML node of fig. 3B.

The method includes transmitting an indication of the ability to generate a random bit sequence to a data node at block 310.

Any suitable signaling may be used to send the indication of the capability. The signaling used to send the indication of capability may depend on whether the ML node is an access node or a UE. For example, if the ML node is a UE, the indication may be sent using Radio Resource Control (RRC) signaling. If the ML node is an access node, the indication may be sent using System Information (SI).

At block 312, the method includes receiving one or more parameters from a data node for generating a random bit sequence. The received parameters conform to the indicated capabilities.

At block 314, the method includes receiving a random bit sequence from the data node, wherein the random bit sequence includes training data for training an ML model in the ML node.

The ML node may annotate the received random bit sequence to generate annotated data for training the ML model. The ML node may annotate the received random bit sequence with a random bit sequence generated by the ML node using the received one or more parameters.

The ML node may store a received original signal that includes the transmitted bit sequence. The stored raw signal may be used as an input for training the ML model.

In some examples, the ML node may demodulate the received signal and record a random sequence of received bits after demodulation. This may enable omitting the step of physical layer mapping.

In some examples, the ML node may send a request for a random bit sequence to the data node. The request may include the RNG algorithm to be used, the seed of the RNG algorithm to be used, the length of the random bit sequence to be generated, the transmit power level to be used for the signal comprising the random bit sequence, and/or any other suitable information. The data node may generate and transmit a random bit sequence in response to the received request.

The ML model may be trained to estimate the probability of the received bits, or perform any other suitable function. The trained ML model may be used for channel estimation or equalization, or any other suitable purpose. The trained ML model may be used to improve reliability of communications between the ML node and other nodes in the network.

Examples of the present disclosure may be used to obtain training data from a real network. This facilitates fine tuning of the machine learning model at the deployment location. Examples of the present disclosure enable training data to be collected with little adverse impact on the network.

Fig. 4 illustrates an exemplary method that may be implemented in examples of the present disclosure. Fig. 4 shows signaling between a data node and an ML node. In this example, the data node may be a UE and the ML node may be an access node. In other examples, the data node may be an access node and the ML node may be a UE.

At block 400, the method includes configuring a random bit sequence. The configuration may include indicating, by the ML node, the ability of the ML node to generate a random bit sequence. The indication is signaled from the ML node to the data node. The indication ensures that the same procedure can be used to generate random bit sequences in both the data node and the ML node.

The configuration may further comprise transmitting, by the data node to the ML node, parameters to be used for generating the random bit sequence. The transmitted parameters may conform to the indicated capabilities.

This configuration may ensure that the same RNG procedure is used by both the data node and the ML node. This may enable both the data node and the ML node to generate the same random bit sequence.

At block 402, the data node sends a random bit sequence to the ML node. The random bit sequence is generated using RNG parameters already agreed during the configuration block. The data node may generate and transmit the random bit sequence in response to a request from the ML node or in response to any other suitable trigger.

At block 404, the ML node trains an ML model using the received random bit sequence. Since both the data node and the ML node can generate the same random bit sequence, the noisy received signal comprising the random bit sequence can be annotated with the corresponding random bit sequence generated by the ML node. The annotated data may then be used to train and/or calibrate the ML model. The ML model may be trained to perform any suitable function.

Fig. 5 illustrates another exemplary method that may be implemented in examples of the present disclosure. Fig. 5 shows signaling between a data node and an ML node. In this example, the data node may be a UE and the ML node may be an access node. Or the data node may be an access node and the ML node may be a UE. In some cases, the UE may establish a connection with the access node for the purpose of training ML. The connection may enable training data to be collected.

The data nodes and ML nodes may be preconfigured with RNG algorithms prior to performing the method of fig. 5. The RNG algorithm and/or the manner in which the RNG algorithm is used to generate the random bit sequence may be pre-agreed upon by the network provider or any other suitable entity. Any suitable RNG may be used in the practice of the present disclosure.

In some examples, it may be pre-agreed to generate a random bit sequence by specifying an RNG that can be seeded and always produce the same bit sequence using a given seed. In some examples, a bit sequence of a particular length may be specified. The bit length may be specified along with the seed and RNG. The predefined sequence or RNG may be stored by the respective node with its hardware.

At block 500, the method includes exchanging a capability indication between a data node and an ML node. The capability indication enables the data node and the ML node to learn from each other that they can generate a random bit sequence for training data. The capability indication enables the data node and the ML node to learn from each other the limitations they have in generating a random bit sequence for training data. In some examples, the capability indication may include that the ML node may indicate to the data node the capability of the ML node to generate the random bit sequence. Similarly, the data node may indicate to the ML node the ability of the data node to generate a random bit sequence.

The signaling used by the node to indicate the capability may depend on the type of node. For example, the UE may indicate capabilities during connection establishment. The indication may be made using RRC signaling such as RRC UE capabilities. The access node may use SI to indicate the capability.

At block 502, an initial configuration of data nodes and ML nodes is performed. The initial configuration may include transmitting, by the data node to the ML node, parameters to be used to generate the random bit sequence. The parameters conform to the capabilities indicated at block 500. The parameters may include the type of RNG to be used, the initial state of the RNG, how the transmission of the random bit sequence is scheduled, when the transmission of the random bit sequence is scheduled, or any other suitable information.

At block 504, training data is sent from the data node to the ML node. The training data comprises one or more random bit sequences, wherein the random bit sequences have been generated according to the transmitted parameters and the indicated capabilities.

In examples of the present disclosure, an ML node may request data to be generated and scheduled for transmission. That is, the node that is to receive the data requests the data that is to be generated and scheduled for transmission.

The training data may be scheduled for transmission in any suitable manner. In some examples, training data may be scheduled on demand in response to a request from an ML node. In such examples, training data may be scheduled using control signaling such as media access control elements (MAC CEs) or downlink/uplink (DL/UL) control channels.

In some examples, training data may be scheduled and transmitted using a predefined pattern. The predefined pattern may be based on the indicated capabilities, or any other suitable information that has been exchanged in the configuration.

In some examples, training data may be sent to two or more ML nodes. For example, data may be broadcast on the DL. This may be the case if two or more ML nodes have requested data from a data node.

In some cases, training data may be broadcast without the ML node specifically requesting the data. In this case, the ML node (such as the UE) can read from the SI when and where the training data will be sent. The ML node can read this information without connecting to the cell. In this case, the ML node may acquire the training data by listening only to the broadcasted training data.

The random bit sequence including the training data may completely or partially replace the physical layer process. Fig. 6 shows an example of a mapping of a generated random bit sequence to a physical layer.

At block 506, the ML node receives the transmitted training data. The received training data comprises a random bit sequence generated by the data node.

The data node may learn the scheduled transmission of training data. Any suitable signaling may be used to make the data node aware of the scheduled transmission of training data. For example, downlink Control Information (DCI) or Uplink Control Information (UCI) may include information indicating when transmission of training data is scheduled.

The data node also knows to process the received data as training data if the data node knows the scheduled transmission of the training data. For example, the received training data need not be passed to upper layers, but may be prepared and recorded for calibration or training of the ML.

At block 508, the ML node trains or calibrates the ML model used by the ML node. The ML node trains or calibrates the ML model using the received signal and the random bit sequence generated by the ML node.

The ML node may use a random bit sequence generated by the ML node as a tag and a corresponding received original signal as an input to the ML model. This provides real data from the network that can be used for supervised training of the ML model.

If a differentiable model of a complete ML node is available, the received data may be used in a similar manner to train any portion of the ML node. In particular, since the ML node knows the bits sentAnd it has recorded the received signalThe ML model can now be trained accordingly. Fig. 6 illustrates an exemplary physical layer mapping that may be used in some examples of the present disclosure. This shows the physical layer mapping for both layers.

Fig. 6 illustrates a portion of a physical layer processing method. In the standard physical layer processing method, the transport blocks are processed to generate concatenated code blocks. The processing may include Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) attachment, graph selection, code block segmentation, channel coding, rate matching, code block concatenation, and/or any other suitable processing. For simplicity, these processes are not shown in fig. 6.

In the standard physical processing layer approach, the concatenated code blocks are scrambled at block 600 and then modulated at block 602 before layer mapping at block 604, antenna port mapping at block 606, and mapping to Resource Blocks (RBs) at block 610.

However, in the examples of the present disclosure, the random bit sequence y is generated by the random number generator 610. The random bit sequence may be mapped directly to symbols on a given RB or to a Transport Block (TB) payload. For example, if the generated bit sequence is to be used as training data for a fully learned ML model, the transmitted sequence may fully replace the payload data. That is, all physical layer processing methods before modulation may be omitted. This provides a flexible process that can be used for a variety of different receiver algorithms.

In the example of fig. 6, RNG algorithm 610 has been designated during the capability indication and/or reconfiguration process. The initial state of the RNG algorithm 610 may be agreed upon by the data node and the ML node. In some cases, this initial state represented by the seed may be agreed upon during initial configuration or during any other suitable process. In this case, the initial state of the RNG algorithm is denoted by X. The number of bits to be transmitted may also be agreed upon by the data node and the ML node. The number of bits to be transmitted may be agreed upon during initial configuration or during any other suitable procedure. In this case, the number of bits to be transmitted by the RNG algorithm is defined byAnd (3) representing. The RNG thus provides as output a random bit sequence y. The random bit sequence y is known to both the ML node and the data node. As shown in fig. 6, the random bit sequence y is mapped directly to the transmitted symbol and all earlier standard physical layer blocks have been skipped.

The ML node knows that blocks of the physical layer procedure have been omitted. The data node knows the random bit sequence transmitted. The data node may record the received bits after demodulation. Received bitsRandom bit sequences of the same length as generatedAnd (5) associating. This may be used for training and/or calibration of the machine learning model.

The ML node may also store the received original signal. The original signal may be stored after a transformation such as FFT is performed on the original signal. The original signal may be stored with associated control information such as DMRS configuration. The original signal and the transmitted bit sequence comprise training or calibration data for the ML model.

Fig. 7 illustrates an exemplary method that may be used in some examples of the present disclosure. In this case, the access node requests training data from the UE. In this case, the access node is an ML node and the UE is a data node.

At block 700, a connection establishment is established between an access node and a UE. During connection establishment, the individual nodes' ability to generate random bit sequences may be shared.

At block 702, an access node sends a request for training data to a UE. The request may be sent when the access node needs training data. The request may be sent some time after the connection is established. The request for training data may also include information such as RNG index, random seed, amount of data required, and/or any other suitable information. In some examples, the request may include a power level to be used to obtain data having different signal-to-noise ratios. In other examples, other information may be included within the request.

At block 704, the access node provides scheduling grants to the UE for transmission of the requested training data. A Physical Downlink Control Channel (PDCCH) may be used for scheduling grants.

At block 706, the UE sends the requested training data to the access node. The requested training data comprises a random bit sequence, wherein the random bit sequence is generated using parameters agreed during connection establishment. The random bit sequence may be transmitted with the requested RNG seed and/or other suitable information.

In some examples, the random bit sequence may include completely random bits. In other examples, the random bit sequence may include one or more regular portions, such as a regular header. The use of fully random bits may be preferred as this may provide more robust training of the ML model.

Training data is transmitted in accordance with scheduling grants provided by the access node. A Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) may be used for training data.

Once the random bit sequence is received by the access node, the access node will store the received data vector. The data vector, as well as the RNG index and seed, may be used to reconstruct the original bit sequence that was sent so that this can be used to train the ML model.

At block 708, additional transmission of the requested training data to the access node is performed. The requested training data may be transmitted in as many time slots as requested. RNG states may be maintained between time slots. To maintain the proper state of the RNG, the RNG cannot be used for any other content between the generation of the corresponding random number sequences.

In the example of fig. 7, the access node is an ML node and the UE is a data node. In other examples, the access node may be a data node and the UE may be an ML node. In this case a method similar to the one shown will be used, but a request for data is sent by the UE and a random bit sequence is sent by the access node.

Fig. 8 illustrates an exemplary method that may be implemented in examples of the present disclosure. In this example, the access node requests training data. In this example, the access node is an ML node and the UE is a data node. In other examples, the access node may be a data node and the UE may be an ML node.

At block 800, a configuration procedure is performed between an access node and a UE. The configuration may include parameters agreed by the access node and the UE to be used for generating the random bit sequence.

At block 802, the access node requests training data. The access node may send a request for training data to the UE. In response to the request, at block 804, the UE transmits a time slot for training data. The training data comprises a random bit sequence generated from agreed parameters.

At block 806, the access node receives a random bit sequence. At block 812, the access node may store any suitable data related to the received random bit sequence. In some examples, the access node may store the received original signal. The original signal may be stored after the FFT has been performed. The original signal may be stored with an associated demodulation reference signal (DMRS) or other configuration information.

At block 814, the stored data is used to construct a training data set. The training data set may include the original received signal as the input signal and the known transmitted bits as the tag.

At block 808, a determination is made as to whether more training data is needed. If more training data is needed, the method returns to block 802 and the access node requests more data.

If no more training data is needed, the method proceeds to block 810 and the ML model is trained. The ML model is trained using the data set constructed at block 814. The ML model may be trained in a supervised manner.

At block 816, the method provides as output a refinement model or a trained ML model.

In examples of the present disclosure, data traffic will take precedence over the collection of training data. Thus, the data node may reject the request for training data. The data node may reject the request using any suitable mechanism. In some examples, the data node may reject the request for training data simply by ignoring the request for training data. In such an example, the request for training data may be associated with an expiration time. If training data is not received by the expiration time, the request is considered to be denied.

In an example where the data node is a UE, instead of transmitting training data, the UE may reject the request for training data by transmitting a scheduling request for new uplink data. Thus, the access node, which is an ML node, determines that training data is not desired.

In some examples, a physical layer priority flag may be used to identify training data as low priority. In such an example, the ML node would only request training data if there is no other useful data within the queue.

The respective node may also be configured to determine when there is a sufficiently low congestion level in the network so that resources for generating ML training data may be consumed. Any suitable means may be used to determine the congestion level. In some examples, the congestion level may be determined based on a time window within which usage of resources is measured. If the use of the resources is below a predefined threshold, transmission of training data is allowed.
